promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 10 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: Stick to the planned three runs plus rest days; daily running could overwhelm a new runner.

flags.title: Fatigue
flags.detail: watch for increased soreness after the long run.  Heart‑rate drift: keep HR below 150 on easy runs.  Cadence consistency: maintain 340–350 spm.  Calf tightness: watch for lingering tightness after each run.  Pace reliability: verify race‑pace segments feel sustainable.

answers.question: I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?
answers.answer: No, you don't need to run every day next week.  The build phase works best with rest days to recover and allow your body to adapt.  Keep the schedule of three runs plus rest days.

new.analysis:
The athlete is new to running, having only started in August.  He did three walk‑run sessions last week and has no pain.  His goal is to run the whole 5K on Nov 15, which is 10 weeks out, placing him in the build phase.  He asks whether he should add daily runs next week to get there faster.

We keep the build approach: 80% of the week should stay easy volume, with only one quality session and a recovery.  Adding daily running would increase fatigue and risk overreaching, especially for a beginner.  Rest days are important for adaptation and injury prevention.  Therefore we advise against daily running.

We also monitor a few key signals for this week: general fatigue from increased volume, heart‑rate trends to ensure we stay in zone 1‑2, calf tightness noted in the last week, and the consistency of the 5K race‑pace work.  These will guide next weeks' adjustments.

The plan is consistent with the build phase: easy runs on Mon and Wed, a lighter recovery Friday, and a single quality session Saturday.  Each run’s purpose is stated, and distances are expressed in kilometres.

No red flags were observed, so no safety callouts are needed.

days.line: Mon 2026-08-31: easy, 6 km, keep HR under 150, gentle volume.
Wed 2026-09-02: easy, 5 km, steady pacing, keep HR below 150.

days.line: Sat 2026-09-05: quality, 6 km, warm‑up 1 km easy, then 4 km at 5K race pace, cool 1 km.
